A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTRL. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, proofs, tables and figures. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original conditional image-generation experiments on compressibility and joint compressibility/aesthetics, with quantitative results, generated images and a guidance-strength analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains the image experiments and adds original DNA enhancer-generation results in Appendix F and image-quality evaluations in Appendix G.3.1.

M1.justification: CTRL retains its classifier reward, linear-embedding augmentation, KL-regularized objective and direct-backpropagation procedure. Algorithm 2 moves to Appendix C without substantive changes. The DNA experiment explicitly uses the same augmentation procedure with a different diffusion backbone.

E1.justification: v2 adds biological sequence design using approximately 700,000 length-200 DNA enhancers, conditioning on accessibility in HepG2 and SKNSH cells (Appendix F). This substantially extends the image-only coverage of v1; both original image tasks remain.

E2.justification: Both image comparisons expand from DPS alone to Reconstruction Guidance, Classifier-Free Guidance, SMC, MPGD and SVDD. DPS is retained under the Reconstruction Guidance name. Classifier-Free Guidance, explicitly excluded from v1's experiments, is now evaluated alongside three additional comparators.

E3.justification: The new enhancer protocol discretizes both controls into ten classes, evaluates extreme SKNSH conditions across HepG2 classes, and measures SKNSH score differences and Kendall's tau. Image evaluation adds BRISQUE and CLIPScore, and the classifier-free baseline introduces synthetic-triplet augmentation. The original image-training hyperparameters and classifier splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.3.1 adds a focused analysis of image quality and text-image alignment alongside conditioning success. The original DPS guidance-strength sweep, confusion matrix and generated-image grids are retained or relocated, rather than newly added ablations.

E5.justification: v2 introduces ± uncertainty values for image accuracies and several new metrics; v1 reports point estimates only. Neither the meaning of these uncertainty values nor run/seed counts is specified, so this establishes additional reporting, not additional repeated experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, enhancer and image-quality results. For retained image comparisons, DPS/Reconstruction Guidance compressibility macro F1 changes from 0.44 to 0.45, and CTRL multitask aesthetics macro F1 changes from 0.92 to 0.93; CTRL accuracies remain unchanged. The new enhancer comparison reports SKNSH differences of 0.299, 0.210 and 0.090 for CTRL, Reconstruction Guidance and Classifier-Free Guidance, respectively.

T1.justification: New Appendix B explicitly defines the discrete MDP's state/action spaces, identity transitions, terminal reward and policy-level KL objective. This is a limited addition to the formal setup. The main target distribution, theorems, lemmas and proofs remain substantively unchanged, with proofs moved from Appendix C to E.

C1.justification: The central RL-conditioning, conditional-sampling and sample-efficiency claims remain. The conclusion extends the stated empirical contribution to biological sequence design, replacing v1's description of scientific applications as future work.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands limitations and interpretation through discussions of classifier-free augmentation errors and prompt diversity, multitask computational demands and task balancing, memory scaling, and guidance/KL tradeoffs (Appendices G.1 and H). Earlier discussions of classifier errors and reconstruction-guidance failures remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access information, a reproducibility statement, baseline augmentation instructions, sequence-classifier architecture and training hyperparameters, and approximately 20/200 A100 GPU-hour costs for the image tasks. Most original image implementation details are retained. However, v1's explicit 512×512 resolution and negative-JPEG-kilobyte definition of compressibility are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 broadens its positioning to sampling and decoding approaches through SMC, SVDD and MPGD, and adds substantial biological-design context covering enhancer design, sequence diffusion and accessibility prediction. The earlier classifier-guidance, classifier-free-guidance and RL positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Numerous main-text paragraphs are condensed or rewritten, planning details move from Section 4.2 into Appendix C, and experimental documentation is reorganized into dedicated baseline, image, sequence and visualization subsections. Separate MDP and limitations appendices and a reproducibility statement substantially reshape the exposition.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates the compressibility histogram and results into Figure 1, expands comparison tables, and moves the confusion matrix into the appendix. It adds an MDP diagram, enhancer results and boxplots, image-quality results and sequence-detail tables. The conference template also changes typography and layout throughout; existing image grids are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 relied on DPS alone for experimental comparison and deferred scientific applications. v2 addresses these important evidence gaps with four additional image baselines, including classifier-free guidance, and computational enhancer-design experiments. Image-quality checks, implementation information and substantive limitations further strengthen evaluation and transparency. Undefined uncertainty notation, incomplete protocol details and omitted compression specifications remain weaknesses, but the broader validation provides a substantial net improvement.
